en.title: Report the Sum After Each Replace-All Query
en.description:
Each query old new replaces every element of the current array that equals old with new, then outputs the sum after the change. Queries take effect cumulatively; when old=new or old is not currently present, the array does not change.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, editorial and tests; missing original bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the statement.
en.input: The first line contains n q, the second line contains n integers, followed by q lines of old new. The original statement gives no value bounds; on this site 0≤n,q≤200000, and all array and query values are in −10^9..10^9.
en.output: Output the sum after each change, one per line in query order, for q lines in total; when q=0, output an empty line.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 6 / 6 / -3; 0 / 0 / 2; and an empty line, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Keep a frequency table and the current sum. When old≠new, take the frequency c of old, increase the sum by (new−old)c, then merge c into the frequency of new; when the two values are equal, leave the state unchanged.
